## In the MRP

The parameter $n_t$ measures the gross financing need as a share of gross domestic product. It is calculated as the sum of long-term debt divided by its weighted average maturity, short-term debt, and the headline deficit. The data comes from the [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) World Economic Outlook, [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd), and national debt management offices. Analysts cross-check this value against the gross financing need published in [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd) Article IV reports or the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd). This variable acts as the model's state variable. It is compared with the edges of the fragile band to classify the country as safe, fragile, or distressed.

## In the DAP

The discretionary adjustments process for refinancing need covers task R1*. It addresses three issues. R1-E checks for missing or distorted components. Red flags include unavailable maturity or bill data, with the OECD Global Debt Report serving as a fallback. It also flags debt growing faster than deficits explain by more than one percent of gross domestic product per year, and contingent liabilities migrating onto the sovereign. R1-T checks for shifts in financing behavior. Red flags include a rising share of bills or a lower maturity target, and changes in or depletion of the treasury cash buffer. The anchored corner is $n_t$ net of the cash buffer. R1-A checks for debt not exposed to the market. Red flags include official loans, program financing, and captive holdings. The anchored corner is the market-held refinancing need. A parameter move changes values under the standard definition, never the definition itself.

## Methods by Document Type

### [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) assesses debt sustainability using debt-to-gross domestic product ratios and public investment levels. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 42">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports general government debt stocks and deficits, as well as tax arrears and shadow economy estimates, which impact long-term fiscal sustainability and refinancing risks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 15">ⓘ</button>
- The document does not explicitly detail gross financing needs as a single figure. However, it notes that the rise in debt and deficit implies increasing rollover needs, though the debt stock remains very low. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability is analyzed based on the projected decline in the debt-to-gross domestic product ratio. The report highlights the role of primary surpluses and gross domestic product growth in reducing debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability is monitored via the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring Forecast, which projects gross debt trajectories and analyses structural primary balances. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- The report details the composition of public debt and financing needs, including the impact of high interest payments and the use of European Union loans for defence. It does not explicitly compute gross financing needs but provides the underlying debt and deficit figures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The document notes that public investment is expected to increase significantly due to defence equipment purchases, raising total public investment above 5 percent of gross domestic product. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 32" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Finland_2026-06-03, p. 32">ⓘ</button>
- The MRP inputs for refinancing need are derived from the projected general government debt stock, interest expenditure, and primary balance. The document provides explicit projections for debt-to-gross domestic product and interest payments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/France_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Debt and deficit figures are sourced from the Commission Spring 2026 Forecast and national accounts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Germany_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The document provides general government gross debt as a percentage of gross domestic product, with projections for 2026 and 2027. It details the composition of debt reduction, attributing it to primary surpluses and nominal growth. It also reports on non-performing loan stocks held by banks and credit servicers, linking them to the financial sector's health and sovereign exposure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 38-39, p. 61-62" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Greece_2026-06-03, p. 6, p. 38-39, p. 61-62">ⓘ</button>
- The document details the debt stock, including holdings by insurers and pension funds, and discusses the cost of servicing public debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 76" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Italy_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 76">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports general government debt-to-gross domestic product ratios and gross financing needs are implicit in the deficit and debt figures. It notes the activation of the national escape clause. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Latvia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability analysis is based on the Commission’s Spring 2026 Forecast. The report notes significant stock-flow adjustments affecting the debt trajectory. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 31" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Ireland_2026-06-03, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- Refinancing needs are influenced by rising public debt and defence spending. Domestic bank lending and capital market depth are key constraints on financing behavior. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 61, p. 66" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Lithuania_2026-06-03, p. 61, p. 66">ⓘ</button>
- Debt stock and composition are discussed in Annex 2, referencing general government debt-to-gross domestic product ratios and projections. Specific details on maturity profiles or short-term debt shares are not extensively detailed in the main summary but are noted as part of the debt sustainability framework. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- The report provides gross and net general government debt figures, household debt ratios, and information on contingent liabilities related to energy companies. It discusses the structure of public debt and financing needs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The document reports gross general government debt levels. It does not provide detailed maturity profiles or gross financing need figures, but the low debt level suggests manageable refinancing needs under normal market conditions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability analysis incorporates the trajectory of public debt reduction and the role of EU-funded investment in shaping future financing needs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 41" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- Debt projections are based on primary balance developments, interest rates, and stock-flow adjustments including public investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 39" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The report addresses the current account deficit and government debt dynamics, noting the persistent deficits and rising debt levels. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 3, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- Debt sustainability is assessed through the evolution of the debt-to-gross domestic product ratio, public investment levels, and stock-flow adjustments. The document does not provide explicit gross financing need figures but implies manageable refinancing conditions given the declining debt ratio and ECB support. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 35">ⓘ</button>

### [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd)

- The document cites general government debt and deficit figures from [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd) and projections from the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- The document cites general government debt and deficit figures from [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd) and projections from the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The document cites general government debt and deficit figures from [Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd) and projections from the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) Spring 2026 Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- Debt projections are based on the assumption that nominal gross domestic product continues to grow faster than interest payments and that primary surpluses are maintained. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt increased from 23.8% of GDP at the end of 2024 to 29.9% of GDP at the end of 2025. The Commission Spring 2026 Forecast projects the debt-to-GDP ratio to increase to 32.3% by the end of 2026 and to 35.5% by the end of 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- The increase in the debt ratio in 2025 mainly reflects capital injections into the Bulgarian Energy Holding and the Bulgarian Development Bank. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt increased from 23.5% of GDP at the end of 2024 to 24.1% at the end of 2025. It is projected to increase to 26.9% by the end of 2026 and 30.5% by the end of 2027. The increases reflect high deficits and positive stock-flow adjustments in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt decreased from 93.5% of GDP in 2024 to 89.7% of GDP in 2025. The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) projects a further decrease to 87.6% in 2026 and 86.0% in 2027. This decline is attributed to persistent primary surpluses and a favorable interest-growth differential. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt increased to 61.4% of GDP at the end of 2025 and is projected to reach 66.9% by the end of 2027. The increase reflects persistent deficits and interest expenditures growing faster than the economy. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt decreased from 66.4% of GDP at the end of 2024 to 65.7% at the end of 2025, projected to decrease to 64.9% in 2026 and 65.1% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovenia_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- General government debt decreased from 101.6% of GDP at the end of 2024 to 100.7% of GDP at the end of 2025. The Commission projects the debt-to-GDP ratio to decrease to 99.6% by the end of 2026 and 98.9% by the end of 2027. The decrease reflects nominal GDP growth outpacing the cost of debt servicing. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>

### [Post-Programme Surveillance Report](../document-types/post-programme-surveillance-report.qmd)

- Debt sustainability and refinancing risks are assessed using data from the Debt Sustainability Monitor 2025 and national debt management offices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 10, p. 14, p. 18" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 5, p. 10, p. 14, p. 18">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd)

- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) assesses debt sustainability analysis including gross and net debt metrics. It accounts for the composition of debt across federal and regional governments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 44-45" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 44-45">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) builds the gross financing need from the debt stock, short-term debt, weighted average maturity, and deficit. It cross-checks against published data on government debt and interest payments. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that debt dynamics are currently favourable as expected nominal growth is well above interest rates on government debt. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 53" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 53">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) reports general government debt according to the Maastricht definition and provides data on non-performing loans and corporate indebtedness. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 10" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 10">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) analyzes debt trajectories using gross debt data from the [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) Economic Outlook database, incorporating assumptions about interest rates, growth, and discretionary fiscal measures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) assesses debt metrics including both Maastricht-defined gross debt and broader general government gross debt. It highlights the importance of monitoring contingent liabilities from state-owned enterprises and climate risks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) projects debt based on gross general government debt and Maastricht definition debt. It assesses the long-term trajectory of debt under different policy and demographic scenarios. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) assesses gross general government debt using the Maastricht definition and net debt, noting that interest payments are rising and repayment of crisis-related debt will start in 2028. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 26" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 26">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) assesses refinancing risks by examining the weighted average maturity of public debt (approx. 19 years) and the share of official lending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 32">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that gross refinancing needs are currently near 25% of GDP and the term structure of outstanding debt is near the euro-area average at close to 8 years. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 38" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 38">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) analyzes debt sustainability under current policies, fiscal reforms, and fiscal plus structural reforms scenarios, projecting debt-to-GNI* ratios up to 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 34" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 34">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) reports general government gross debt and net financial liabilities. It notes the low level of public debt but projects an increase in the coming years. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 12" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 12">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that debt sustainability is sensitive to interest rate movements and growth trajectories, projecting general government gross debt (Maastricht) to rise from 46.9% of GDP in 2025 to 50.3% in 2027. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) evaluates fiscal sustainability through stylised debt scenarios, projecting debt-to-GDP ratios under different policy assumptions, including pension reforms and defence spending increases. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) analyzes the effectiveness of the debt brake using a fiscal reaction function estimated over 1995-2024. It finds that the primary balance became more stabilising in response to debt levels after EU accession negotiations began, but not after the introduction of the debt brake. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 50" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 50">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) assesses gross general government debt using the Maastricht definition. The debt-to-GDP ratio would significantly increase in the 2040s under current policies due to aging costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 12, p. 8, p. 46" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 12, p. 8, p. 46">ⓘ</button>

## Institutions and Data Sources

- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: Issued the Country Reports and assessed debt sustainability. It activated the national escape clause for defence spending for [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd), [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd), [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd), and [Austria](../countries/austria.qmd). It monitors the [European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd) loan availability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 35, p. 42" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 35, p. 42">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 37">ⓘ</button>
- **[Eurostat](../institutions/eurostat.qmd)**: Provides data on gross general government debt and deficit statistics cited in the reports. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: Activated the national escape clause for defence spending. Made financial assistance available under the Security Action for Europe instrument for [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd), [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd), [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd), and [Cyprus](../countries/cyprus.qmd). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Bulgaria_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 6" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Estonia_2026-06-03, p. 6">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd)**: Referenced in the context of backstop eligibility and compliance with EU fiscal frameworks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 35" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The European Commission assesses the implementation of country-specific recommendations (CSRs) and provides forecasts for economic and fiscal indicators. It evaluates Belgium’s progress in structural reforms and compliance with EU fiscal rules. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24-29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 24-29">ⓘ</button>
- **[Council of the EU](../institutions/council-of-the-eu.qmd)**: The Council of the European Union adopted a recommendation endorsing Belgium’s medium-term fiscal structural plan and a revised recommendation under Article 126(7) TFEU regarding the excessive deficit procedure. It also activated the national escape clause for defence spending. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- **[European Investment Bank](../institutions/european-investment-bank.qmd)**: The European Investment Bank provides funding for various projects in Belgium, including energy efficiency renovations, sustainable transport, and social housing. For instance, Brussels received EUR 475 million from the EIB for electric buses and metro/tram sets. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 72" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 72">ⓘ</button>

- **[European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd)**: The [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd) cut policy rates since June 2024, which has supported private consumption and investment in [Finland](../countries/finland.qmd) by lowering borrowing costs <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 20" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 20">ⓘ</button>

- **[European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)**: The document references [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd) data and policies, such as the European Union fiscal framework and the European Union's Restoration Regulation, which impact Finnish fiscal and environmental policy <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 116" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 116">ⓘ</button>
